dedupe_keys.name: hcrl car hacking dataset can traffic with dos fuzzy and spoofing attacks korea university

description: The HCRL Car-Hacking Dataset contains CAN traffic logged through the OBD-II port of a real vehicle while message injection attacks were carried out. It has four attack types: denial of service (injecting CAN ID 0000 every 0.3 ms), fuzzy (random IDs and data every 0.5 ms), and spoofing of the drive gear and the RPM gauge (injecting specific IDs every 1 ms). Each dataset holds 300 intrusions of 3 to 5 seconds, and records have a timestamp, CAN ID, data length code, eight data bytes and an attack flag. The lab releases the data for academic purposes and asks users to cite its papers on CNN-based detection (Vehicular Communications, 2020) and GAN-based detection (PST 2018). Coverage: one vehicle. Format and access: download link on the page. Licence and cost: free for academic use with citation. Caveats: single vehicle and synthetic attacks. It supports digital twin and cascading failure studies of vehicle cyber attacks. It relates to the can-train-and-test dataset in the catalogue.
